extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the MRC Career Development Award (fellowship) hosted by eligible UK research organisations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the MRC Career Development Award (a fellowship to support transition to independence). Covers eligibility, required statements, section-level assessment guidance, permitted costs, partner/collaboration requirements and the assessment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: degree and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to apply for the career development award you must: have completed a PhD or equivalent; have the skills and experience that match those of the ‘transition to independence’ career stage in the MRC applicant skills and experience criteria, such as showing evidence of career progression and productivity across past appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have your own research plans that do not significantly overlap with those of your current group leaders or proposed sponsors and have the support of an eligible research organisation. There are no eligibility rules based on age or years of postdoctoral experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: exclusions and application limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not eligible to apply if: you have applied for this MRC fellowship within the last year; you have applied for this MRC fellowship twice; you have applied for any UKRI fellowship and your application is being assessed; you have applied for an MRC new investigator research grant and your application is being assessed; you have been awarded an MRC NIRG or a comparable fellowship or new investigator grant from any organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may only apply twice for any MRC fellowship, regardless of extent of changes to the application. You cannot hold a salaried position and a fellowship at the same time — you will need to give up the permanent position or change to a proleptic appointment if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and remit of allowable research
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome applications from across all areas of our remit to improve human health, ranging from basic studies with relevance to disease mechanisms to translational and developmental clinical research. Interdisciplinary approaches and global health research are welcome if aligned with MRC’s core remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science areas include infections and immunity, molecular and cellular medicine, population and systems medicine, neurosciences and mental health, translation, global health, methodology, public health. Global health proposals should align with MRC’s remit from discovery to early translational research. New longitudinal population studies require LPS-SAP approval before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the fellowship funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The career development award will cover the cost of the fellow’s salary and may provide funding for support posts, research consumables, equipment, travel, training, data preservation/sharing/dissemination costs, estates and indirect costs, public partnerships and related activities, and NHS research costs when associated with NHS studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will fund up to five years (pro rata for part-time) and will fund 80% of the full economic cost (100% for permitted exceptions). The award can support a period of research overseas or at a second UK organisation (up to 12 months) and applicants may request joint funding. Requests for support beyond research and innovation associate/technical posts require prior discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the fellowship will not fund
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not fund costs for PhD studentships, publication costs, funding to use as a ‘bridge’ between grants, costs for sponsors or costs for mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and value for money
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit to the amount of funding you can request, however all costs must be fully justified and demonstrate value for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your application must be for an amount that is appropriate to the project and you can justify in order to deliver the objectives of the proposed research. All costs must be fully justified in the resources and costs section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and start date constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The career development award provides support for up to five years (pro rata for part-time fellowships). We expect you to take advantage of the full five years’ funding available; part-time awards are allowed but not because of other professional commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We expect you to start no earlier than April 2026 and no later than September 2026. Any start dates outside these must be discussed with MRC prior to the decision meeting. Applicants may spend up to 12 months at a second organisation; longer overseas periods require prior contact with the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected time and permitted non-fellowship activities
rubrics_metrics.description: This fellowship provides a competitive salary so you can concentrate on research; you may spend up to six hours a week, pro rata for part-time fellowships, on other commitments such as teaching or other funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater flexibility on non-fellowship activities may be allowed during the second half of a fellowship; discuss plans with the programme manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 550. In plain English, provide a summary to identify the most suitable experts to assess your application; the summary may be made publicly available so do not include confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it suitable for a variety of readers (opinion-formers, policymakers, public, wider research community). Guidance for writing the summary: clearly describe context, challenge, aims/objectives, potential applications and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core team composition and role rules
rubrics_metrics.description: List key members of your team and assign roles from fellow, specialist, professional enabling staff, research and innovation associate, technician. Only list one individual as fellow — including more than one will cause application failure at checking stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should not be listed in the core team. Mentors should not be listed in the core team. Core team should be limited to named individuals who will support delivery; resources can be requested for unnamed positions and do not need to be core team members. Public contributors can be added to the 'specialist' role.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and hyperlinks policy
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be included within the word count of the appropriate question section and prioritised to those most pertinent to the application. Hyperlinks can be used in reference information but applications should be self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including references, ensure they are easily identifiable by assessors, formatted appropriately, and use persistent identifiers where possible. Do not use external links to extend your application — assessors are not required to follow links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image use and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Where indicated, you can demonstrate elements of responses in visual form; when including images you must provide a descriptive caption or legend immediately underneath it (counts towards word limit), insert each new image on a new line, and use files smaller than 5MB in specified formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, WEBP, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should only convey important visual information not easily put into words. The following are not permitted and may lead to rejection: sentences or paragraphs of text, tables, excessive quantities of images. A few words are permitted when necessary for clarity (e.g., axis labels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors will look for how the proposed work is of excellent quality and importance within or beyond the field, has potential to advance understanding or generate new knowledge, is timely, and impacts world-leading research, society, the economy or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within Vision also expect identification of direct/indirect beneficiaries, potential improvements in human or population health, and outline of engagement, communication and dissemination plans. References may be included. Word limit: 550.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors will look for a design that is effective and appropriate to achieve objectives, feasible with risks identified and managed, uses a clearly written and transparent methodology, summarises previous work and describes how you will build on it, and will maximise translation of outputs into outcomes and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also expected: demonstrate access to services/facilities/infrastructure/equipment; provide a detailed project plan including milestones and a Gantt chart; explain collaborations and second-host work; justify diversity and inclusion in study population and the use of male/female animals or tissues (or justify not doing so); explain/justify public partnerships. Word limit: 2,800.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and statistical design criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors expect information on reproducibility, reliability and robustness such as statistical analyses and experimental design details not provided in Approach. You should seek professional statistical or other relevant advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sample and effect sizes, planned statistical analyses, models chosen (e.g. animal model, cell line), potential sources of bias and mitigation strategies, and how diversity considerations are reflected in design and analyses. Refer to MRC guidance for examples and tools. Word limit: 500 (varies with project type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors want to know why this fellowship is the right way to develop your career and how you will use it to benefit others: identify career development goals appropriate to the fellowship and how it provides a feasible trajectory to achieve them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how you will instigate positive change in the wider research and innovation community (EDI, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, policy influence, public engagement). Explain how you will ensure continued development of those you manage and how the fellowship will help you acquire research, leadership, communication and management skills. Word limit: 1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant capability to deliver
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors look for evidence that you have relevant experience (appropriate to career stage), the right balance of skills and aptitude to make best use of the funding, contributions to a positive research environment, and appropriate team working or leadership skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Résumé for Research and Innovation (R4RI) format with specified module headings covering contributions to ideas/tools/knowledge, development of others, contributions to wider research community, and contributions to broader societal benefit. Word limit: 1,650 (1,150 for R4RI modules plus optional 500 words additions). Additions should provide context (e.g., career breaks) not extra outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation support statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Head of department must provide a written supporting statement including their name/title and evidence of how the host will support you for career development, protection of your fellowship time, development/training opportunities, and what financial/practical support is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should describe how the research environment contributes to success, evidence of your suitability for an MRC fellowship, and details of any work at another host organisation. Word limit: 1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second host organisation support (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second host (UK or industry) is included, that organisation’s head (or industry equivalent) must provide a statement confirming commitment to support the fellowship, including time protection, development/training opportunities and financial/practical support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable indicate 'N/A'. Word limit: 1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous head of department support statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you recently moved department or plan to undertake the fellowship at a different department to current affiliation, provide a statement from your previous or current head of department assessing your suitability for an MRC fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable indicate 'N/A'. Word limit: 1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one sponsor (a senior member of the host department) must provide a statement (up to 1,000 words) acting as guarantor for quality of proposed research, suitability of candidate and quality of training and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sponsor’s name and position, capacity in which they know the applicant, how long known, views on research ability and suitability, measures of research activity where applicant will be based, and suitability/quality of support and training. The Sponsors section in the application allows up to 3,000 words for multiple sponsors but individual sponsor statements should be concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain proposed mentoring arrangements and, if a mentor is identified, name them and provide a support statement detailing how they will support you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners: definition, restrictions and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Project partners are collaborating persons or organisations providing integral contributions (cash or in-kind) such as staff time, access to equipment, facilities, data, software, materials, recruitment of participants or samples. Project partners must not be core team members or from your organisation, and organisations employing core team members cannot be project partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each partner provide organisation name, contact, type and value of contribution. For audit purposes formal collaboration agreements will be required if funded. Industry partners must complete the Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF) section and provide additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partner letters of support: content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a single PDF with letters/emails of support from each named project partner (English or Welsh only). Each letter/email should include partner name and contact, explain commitment to project, explain the value/relevance/benefit to them, describe additional value they bring, and must not exceed two sides of A4 per project partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters do not need to be on headed paper or include handwritten signatures (electronic signatures acceptable). If partners are responsible for recruiting participants or providing human tissue they must confirm suitability and quantity (not excessive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application includes industry or company project partners you must follow the MRC ICF: confirm whether the research is basic or applied, explain why collaboration cannot be undertaken without the requested UKRI funding, state whether the contribution is fully flexible or gated, outline background IP and terms of access, and outline expected project IP and access terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ICF decision tree and guidance materials (collaboration agreements, definitions, subsidy control, IP arrangements). Enter 'Yes' in the text box for ICF and answer ICF questions 1–9 for each partner. Contact fellows@mrc.ukri.org if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment areas used by reviewers and panels
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment areas we will use are: vision for the fellowship; approach to the fellowship (including reproducibility and statistical design and data management); career development; your capability to deliver the fellowship (skills and experience needed to win support at this career stage); support for the applicant; ethical and responsible research and innovation considerations; resources requested to do the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors will take into account career breaks, flexible working and changes in discipline when assessing career development and capability to deliver. Find assessment questions and criteria under 'Application questions' in How to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are examined for eligibility and scope; expert reviewers are invited to review independently against specified criteria; shortlisted applications go to interview panels; shortlisted applicants are invited to interview and receive reviews and can respond during interview. If not shortlisted you receive reviewers' feedback but cannot respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot nominate reviewers. The process aims to complete assessment within six months; decisions communicated within 10 days of shortlisting/decision meetings. Interview panels make final funding recommendations and MRC makes final funding decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in applications and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of generative AI tools to prepare funding applications is permitted, however caution should be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and panellists are not permitted to use generative AI tools to develop their assessment as this may compromise confidentiality. See MRC policy on use of generative AI for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, diversity and inclusion and flexible working considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC is committed to equality of opportunity and encourages applications from a diverse range of researchers. We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances, including career breaks, support for people with caring responsibilities, flexible working and alternative working patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support during application and assessment. All fellowship awards may be held part-time or within flexible arrangements. Guidance and policies (Concordat, Technician Commitment) are encouraged to be followed. Reviewers will be asked to consider unequal impacts such as COVID-19 related disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusted Research & Innovation (TR&I) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI’s TR&I principles set out expectations of organisations funded by UKRI in relation to due diligence for international collaboration. Applicants for UKRI funding may be asked to demonstrate how proposed projects comply with TR&I, identifying potential risks and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further guidance on TR&I is provided and applicants should identify proportionate controls to reduce risks in international collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/confidential information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or a core team member need to tell us something you wish to remain confidential, email fellows@mrc.ukri.org with subject line including the funding opportunity title, 'sensitive information', and your Funding Service application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical confidential information examples: unavailability dates (parental leave), declaration of interest, additional eligibility details, conflicts of interest for reviewer/panel selection, invited resubmission status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of outcomes and personal data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC/UKRI will publish outcomes of the funding opportunity and if your application is successful, some personal information will be published on the UKRI Gateway to Research. Personal data will be handled in line with UK data protection legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying for a jointly funded fellowship, MRC will share the application and personal information with the joint funder so they can participate in assessment. Read UKRI privacy notice for details.
